requirements.requirement: node1 (VyOS) configured to run a DHCP server on the private network shared with node2/node3
requirements.summary: node1's eth1 (10.50.50.254/24) was configured with VyOS dhcp-server shared-network-name LAN, subnet 10.50.50.0/24, pool 10.50.50.100-200. Config committed to /config/config.boot (cmd-9e910bba49c2405c) and isc-kea-dhcp4-server.service confirmed active (cmd-0a8758fdcf774eb7). After a full node1 reboot, eth1 address, Kea service active state, and connectivity to both clients were re-verified (cmd-d8cce04326d44801), and the post-restart listening-socket snapshot shows kea-dhcp4 bound to 10.50.50.254:67 and 10.100.25.10:67. This demonstrates both configuration and healthy/recovered operation.

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 configured to obtain their private-network address via DHCP from node1 instead of static assignment
requirements.summary: Baseline showed enp8s0 had no address on either node (cmd-8631aa505c1645fa, cmd-e0aad9cf07e24f8e). Ansible installed a DHCP=yes systemd-networkd unit for enp8s0 and both nodes acquired dynamic leases 10.50.50.100/10.50.50.101 from node1 (cmd-763674466c7f4ac6, cmd-8ce38703688a4bbc, cmd-b44c311cfb5146fd). After full reboots of node2 and node3, both re-acquired the same DHCP leases from node1 confirmed via networkctl logs (cmd-395a2d087a3c4f11, cmd-329c00731b914eec, cmd-fae93565e9804aa5, cmd-05c52987c5d2401b), and post-executor socket snapshots show systemd-network bound to the 10.50.50.x DHCP client port on both nodes. No static IP configuration was ever applied — only the DHCP client unit.

requirements.requirement: Implementation delivered as Ansible (playbook run from the designated control node)
requirements.summary: An Ansible inventory and two-play site.yml were authored on node4, the pre-provisioned ansible-core control node, and applied with ansible-playbook (cmd-f81a1b2d5db14b82, cmd-6c7560a8723b493e, cmd-b8877835b3d844b9, cmd-7c726497e68c4f98). A final idempotent re-run after all node restarts (cmd-27e824a3d5f047e7) confirmed 'No configuration changes to commit' on node1 and 'ok' state on clients, showing the playbook is the durable source of the configuration rather than a one-off manual change.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on every managed node (node1-4): pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered service/data/cluster state
requirements.summary: All four nodes show a captured pre-restart boot_id, a reboot command executed and acknowledged, a distinct post-restart boot_id, and recovery evidence: node1 recovered eth1 address/Kea service/ping connectivity (cmd-d8cce04326d44801); node2/node3 recovered their identical DHCP leases from node1 (cmd-329c00731b914eec, cmd-05c52987c5d2401b); node4 recovery is demonstrated by a fully successful ansible-playbook re-run afterward (cmd-27e824a3d5f047e7), which required node4's SSH keys, ansible tooling, and connectivity to all managed nodes to be intact. The fixed after-executor snapshot cross-check confirms all boot-ids changed and no failed services remained on any node.

overall_summary: The task's material outcomes are all satisfied with direct, coherent evidence: node1 runs a Kea DHCPv4 server on the shared private network (10.50.50.0/24), node2 and node3 obtain their private-network address dynamically via a systemd-networkd DHCP client configuration rather than static assignment, and the entire configuration is implemented and reproducible through an Ansible playbook run from the designated control node (node4), confirmed idempotent on a final re-run. The independent provider-wide restart protocol was executed correctly on all four nodes with pre-restart boot-id baselines, acknowledged reboots, changed post-restart boot-ids, and directly observed recovery of DHCP server state, client leases, and connectivity (plus a working idempotent Ansible re-run proving node4's control-plane tooling survived). Operational hygiene is good: initial manual/exploratory VyOS config commands and an SSH-key placement issue (corrected using VyOS's own config-management mechanism to survive reboot) were reasonable troubleshooting for a device with an undocumented config schema, and the final state cleanly matches the Ansible-applied configuration with no residue, failed services, or unaccounted mutations in the before/after snapshots.
limitations: Kea DHCPv4 lease file content was not directly captured (only socket bindings and client-side lease acquisition logs), so server-side lease persistence across the restart was inferred rather than directly observed.

The initial DHCP-server configuration was applied to node1 via manual bash/configure commands before being captured into the Ansible playbook; while the final playbook run reproduces this state idempotently, a small window of manual-only configuration existed.

No evidence explicitly shows node4 lacks a NIC on the private network (consistent with the stated topology), so node4's restart recovery is validated indirectly via playbook re-run success rather than direct private-network state.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewing the chronological command trace: SSH host-key generation and sshd enable/start on node2/node3 (cmd-e30581493ad04eeb, cmd-dca9a3c30f634ffa) were a necessary prerequisite fixing a crash-looping sshd so Ansible could reach the hosts. Adding node4's pubkey to the vyos user (cmd-a565a6cc76324e53) and to root authorized_keys on node2/node3 (cmd-d46ecf28fd74459a, cmd-d00155ece4df4a76) were necessary for control-node access; the node1 key addition was later redone through VyOS's own config-management ('set system login user vyos authentication public-keys', cmd-cd99bbf477e3409e) after discovering the direct file edit didn't survive VyOS's reboot reconciler — a corrective action, not an unnecessary mutation, and it remained in the final state. There was manual/exploratory trial-and-error directly on node1 configuring interfaces and dhcp-server via bash before the correct schema was discovered (cmd-b5069c425c5a4d08 failed, cmd-0d1f4d1d742c4211, cmd-34977f6a7cd64069 failed due to missing subnet-id, cmd-38481ddab11a4a55 finally succeeded) — these manual pre-Ansible experiments on the live VyOS config were reconciled into and superseded by the final Ansible playbook, which is acceptable discovery for a device whose exact config schema wasn't documented, and the final committed state matches the Ansible-managed config. No abandoned files, conflicting services, or residue were found in the before/after diff: temp-file and boot-id differences are expected reboot artifacts, and failed-services lists are empty on all nodes in the final snapshot. The main imperfection is that VyOS DHCP-server/interface config was initially hand-applied via raw configure/commit/save commands directly on node1 rather than exclusively through the Ansible playbook, before being captured into the playbook — a minor deviation from pure IaC discipline, though fully superseded and idempotently reproduced by the final playbook run.
